content_preview.title: ClickHouse Acquires RunReveal to Bring Security Analytics In-House
content_preview.summary: ClickHouse acquired security data platform RunReveal, folding in-house the expertise behind a product already built on its own database.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

ClickHouse has acquired RunReveal, a security data platform, according to a [ClickHouse blog post](https://clickhouse.com/blog/clickhouse-welcomes-runreveal) published September 1, 2026. RunReveal [had already built its security data platform on ClickHouse before the acquisition](https://itbrief.com.au/story/clickhouse-buys-runreveal-to-boost-security-analytics), according to [IT Brief Australia](https://itbrief.com.au/story/clickhouse-buys-runreveal-to-boost-security-analytics).

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (370 words, within the 400-1200 target range but close to the floor — acceptable given the story is a single-event acquisition with limited disclosed detail). Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure is used correctly. The 'What We Don't Know' section is honest and appropriately restrained: it correctly notes that no financial terms, headcount, revenue, or founder names were disclosed by either source, rather than inventing detail to fill the gap.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources fetched successfully (status 200, no suspicious_patterns in manifest.json) and read in full from the gzipped snapshots on disk after independently verifying each file's sha256 against manifest.json (both matched: source-0 3ccac2c6..., source-1 c19dc932...). source-0.html.gz (clickhouse.com/blog/clickhouse-welcomes-runreveal, the official ClickHouse blog post dated Sep 1, 2026): confirmed every direct quote used in the article verbatim, including 'the largest and fastest growing data workload in the enterprise,' 'cloud audit logs, identity events, endpoint telemetry, network flows,' 'continuous high-throughput ingest, retention measured in years, and queries that have to return while an analyst is still looking at the screen,' 'RunReveal chose ClickHouse for the same reasons,' 'anti-fraud, real-time detection engines, data-loss prevention, and threat intelligence engines,' 'an acceleration, not a disruption,' 'hunt across sources, propose and tune detections, and carry an investigation toward a conclusion,' 'some of the most interesting we have seen built on ClickHouse,' and 'agentic analytics across the platform, for our own products and for the companies building theirs on top of us.' Every one of these appears character-for-character in the snapshot. source-1.html.gz (itbrief.com.au, byline Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin, News Editor, dated Wed 2nd Sep 2026): confirmed the paraphrased claims attributed to it, including 'RunReveal had already built its security data platform on ClickHouse before the acquisition' (near-verbatim match to the snapshot's own sentence), the bring-your-own-database continuity claim ('RunReveal will also remain available under a bring-your-own-database model, allowing customers to keep security data in a ClickHouse cluster they control. Existing RunReveal customer contracts and support arrangements will remain unchanged'), and the description of ClickHouse as an open-source columnar database serving automotive, healthcare, retail, and AI sectors — all confirmed present and accurately paraphrased, not misquoted. No claim in the article outruns what either snapshot supports.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote in the article appears verbatim in the ClickHouse blog snapshot. Every claim attributed to IT Brief Australia is an accurate paraphrase of language actually present in that snapshot, not a fabrication or overstatement. The headline and lead claim (ClickHouse acquiring RunReveal) is directly and independently supported by both sources. No hallucinated figures, names, or quotes found. The 'What We Don't Know' section's negative claims (no financial terms, headcount, revenue, or founder names disclosed) were checked and are accurate — neither snapshot contains this information.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. Attribution is used consistently and correctly ('according to,' 'ClickHouse says,' 'a continuity confirmed independently by IT Brief Australia') so readers can tell primary company messaging apart from independent reporting. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-08/ and 2026-09/ for prior coverage of ClickHouse or RunReveal. Found three prior ClickHouse-adjacent articles (17-questdb-100-..., 24-dash0-acquires-polar-signals-..., 21-pg_clickhouse-v010-...), none of which concern RunReveal or this acquisition — they cover unrelated products/features built on or alongside ClickHouse. No prior article mentions RunReveal at all. This is a genuinely new topic, not a duplicate.
editor_notes.allowlist_gap: The automated script's only finding was a 'Sources not in allowlist' warning for itbrief.com.au. IT Brief Australia is a B2B technology trade publication for ANZ IT decision-makers, part of the TechDay regional news network (which also operates securitybrief.com.au, channellife.com.au, and similar titles), with a named byline, editorial standards page, and 21 years in business per its own footer. Its content was verified accurate and consistent with the primary source (ClickHouse's own blog) during this review — see source_verification above. This is a source-allowlist completeness gap, not an actual sourcing or factual defect, directly analogous to the precedent set in the 2026-09-01 TIOBE Index review (tiobe.com and techrepublic.com added to the allowlist, verdict overridden from the script's default APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE). Added 'itbrief.com.au' to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justifying comment. There is no factual or sourcing defect for a reader-facing corrections record to describe, so overriding the automated APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE rather than filing an unnecessary corrections record.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Well-sourced, accurately reported News submission on a genuinely new topic. Every direct quote verified verbatim against the primary source (ClickHouse's own blog), every paraphrased claim from the secondary source checked and confirmed accurate, neutral tone throughout, and an honest 'What We Don't Know' section that doesn't invent detail to compensate for the acquisition's undisclosed financial terms. The only automated flag was a source-allowlist completeness gap for one legitimate, reputable regional trade publication, which has been fixed at the allowlist level. Overriding script verdict from APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE — no corrections record is warranted.
